tracks.title: Foundations and how to read a call
tracks.summary: What SIP is for, which network facts it assumes, and how to read a ladder without inventing rules.

lessons.title: What SIP is for
lessons.summary: SIP creates, changes, and ends sessions, while RTP carries the media those sessions describe.

lessons.title: Ports, transports, and where a request can go
lessons.summary: SIP uses UDP or TCP on 5060 and TLS on 5061, and a request that does not fit one datagram needs a connection.

lessons.title: E.164, sip URIs, and tel URIs
lessons.summary: A global number is written in a tel URI or in a sip URI user part, and E.164 is the numbering plan those digits follow.

lessons.title: How to read an RFC
lessons.summary: A SIP argument cites the RFC number and the section, and the normative sentences outrank a broken example.

lessons.title: The hitchhiker guide is a map
lessons.summary: RFC 5411 is an informational map of the SIP document set, and it does not replace the base specification.

lessons.title: Licenses, codecs, and what you may copy
lessons.summary: Protocol text is under the IETF trust provisions, and codec rights have to be read from the codec's own documents.

lessons.title: Reading the first INVITE
lessons.summary: The first INVITE has a magic-cookie branch, Max-Forwards 70, a From tag, and no To tag.

tracks.title: SIP core: messages, transactions, dialogs
tracks.summary: Roles, methods, headers, transaction timers, dialog identity, and the transports those rules sit on.

lessons.title: Roles a trace is actually showing
lessons.summary: A trace shows a user agent, a proxy, a registrar, a redirect server, or a B2BUA, and products often combine those roles.

lessons.title: Methods and status codes
lessons.summary: The core methods are INVITE, ACK, OPTIONS, BYE, CANCEL, and REGISTER, and status codes fall into six classes.

lessons.title: Headers and compact forms
lessons.summary: Compact header names are aliases from RFC 3261, with a few more aliases defined in the extension RFCs.

lessons.title: Transactions and the branch cookie
lessons.summary: A transaction is identified by the branch, and a retransmission repeats that branch instead of starting a new one.

lessons.title: Dialog identity
lessons.summary: A dialog is identified by Call-ID, the From tag, and the To tag, and the initial request has no To tag.

lessons.title: T1, the transaction timeout, and Timer C
lessons.summary: T1 seeds retransmissions, 64 times T1 ends the transaction, and Timer C is the proxy's longer INVITE arm.

lessons.title: UDP, TCP, TLS, and WebSocket
lessons.summary: The transport is a property of the hop, written in Via, and it changes retransmission and framing rather than the SIP methods.

tracks.title: Call flows that operators actually trace
tracks.summary: The ACK split, route sets, PRACK, UPDATE, session timers, teardown, and transfer.

lessons.title: Two different ACK rules
lessons.summary: The ACK for a non-2xx is hop by hop inside the INVITE transaction, and the ACK for a 2xx is a new end-to-end transaction.

lessons.title: Record-Route and the route set
lessons.summary: A proxy that wants to stay on the dialog prepends a Record-Route URI, and that URI has to contain lr.

lessons.title: PRACK and reliable provisionals
lessons.summary: A provisional response with Require: 100rel is retransmitted until PRACK, and RAck names that exact response.

lessons.title: UPDATE before the INVITE completes
lessons.summary: UPDATE can change the session while the initial INVITE is still outstanding, and it does not use the ACK rules.

lessons.title: Session-Expires and 422
lessons.summary: Session timers name who refreshes the dialog, and 422 tells the caller the interval was below Min-SE.

lessons.title: CANCEL, BYE, and re-INVITE
lessons.summary: CANCEL abandons an unanswered INVITE, BYE ends a confirmed dialog, and re-INVITE changes a dialog that already exists.

lessons.title: REFER and Replaces
lessons.summary: REFER asks another UA to send a request, and Replaces names the dialog that request should take over.

tracks.title: Registration, DNS, and routing
tracks.summary: Bindings, DNS location, loose routing, outbound flows, Path, Service-Route, GRUU, and forking.

lessons.title: REGISTER and bindings
lessons.summary: REGISTER binds an address-of-record to one or more Contacts, and the registrar is a different role from the proxy.

lessons.title: Locating a server with RFC 3263
lessons.summary: RFC 3263 turns a SIP domain into a transport, a port, and an address with NAPTR, SRV, and A or AAAA.

lessons.title: Loose routing and Max-Forwards
lessons.summary: With lr, the Request-URI stays the remote target, each hop pops its own Route, and Max-Forwards of 0 yields 483.

lessons.title: Outbound, reg-id, and keepalives
lessons.summary: RFC 5626 binds a UA instance to one or more flows with reg-id and +sip.instance, and keepalives hold those flows open.

lessons.title: Path and Service-Route
lessons.summary: Path is the inbound vector stored with a binding, and Service-Route is the outbound vector the registrar gives the UA.

lessons.title: GRUU and a single instance
lessons.summary: A GRUU routes to one UA instance, and the registrar returns it as pub-gruu or temp-gruu on the binding.

lessons.title: Forking and early dialogs
lessons.summary: A forking proxy creates one client transaction per binding, and each To tag is a separate early dialog.

tracks.title: SDP and offer/answer
tracks.summary: How to read an SDP body, and how RFC 3264 matches offers to answers without reordering streams.

lessons.title: The lines in an SDP body
lessons.summary: Read v, o, s, c, t, m, and a lines as a session description. RFC 8866 is the current SDP specification.

lessons.title: Same m-lines, same order
lessons.summary: RFC 3264 matches streams by position. The answer has the same number of m-lines, in the same order.

lessons.title: rtpmap names and fmtp parameters
lessons.summary: Match codecs by the rtpmap encoding name. The G.722 rtpmap clock stays 8000.

lessons.title: Direction attributes and hold
lessons.summary: sendrecv, sendonly, recvonly, and inactive are per stream. Hold is commonly sendonly or inactive.

lessons.title: Port 0 rejects a stream
lessons.summary: Port 0 refuses the stream in that slot. The m-line stays, with a protocol and a format list.

lessons.title: Early media and 183
lessons.summary: 183 Session Progress with SDP is the usual early-media pattern. 180 means ringing. A 183 does not always have SDP.

lessons.title: Offer/answer pitfalls in RFC 6337
lessons.summary: RFC 6337 is the usage document for offer/answer mistakes: order, version, delayed offer, and hold.

tracks.title: RTP, codecs, and DTMF
tracks.summary: RTP headers, payload types, codec documents, RTCP, telephone-event, packet time, and one-way audio.

lessons.title: The RTP header
lessons.summary: RTP version 2 carries a sequence number, a timestamp, an SSRC, and a marker bit. SIP does not carry those fields.

lessons.title: Static and dynamic payload types
lessons.summary: RFC 3551 assigns static payload types. Dynamic types are named by rtpmap, and G.722 stays at clock 8000.

lessons.title: G.711, G.729, and Opus
lessons.summary: Choose a codec both sides named. Read RFC 6716 and the Opus license before you draw any legal conclusion.

lessons.title: RTCP sender and receiver reports
lessons.summary: RTCP sender reports and receiver reports describe the RTP flow. A SIP 200 OK does not report loss.

lessons.title: telephone-event and other digit paths
lessons.summary: telephone-event is RFC 4733, a dynamic payload. Events 0 through 15 are DTMF. INFO and KPML are different tools.

lessons.title: ptime, packet rate, and EF
lessons.summary: ptime is SDP. Twenty milliseconds of G.711 is 50 packets per second and 160 bytes of payload, plus headers. Voice sits in the EF class.

lessons.title: One-way audio
lessons.summary: A 200 OK can be perfect while one RTP direction is missing. Read direction, c=, and who is actually sending.

tracks.title: TLS, SRTP, identity, and abuse
tracks.summary: Defensive digest, TLS certificates, SRTP keying, privacy headers, STIR, and abuse controls.

lessons.title: 401, 407, and digest
lessons.summary: A 401 from a UAS is answered with Authorization. A 407 from a proxy is answered with Proxy-Authorization.

lessons.title: TLS and domain certificates
lessons.summary: SIP over TLS is RFC 3261 section 18. The certificate has to identify the SIP domain, per RFC 5922.

lessons.title: SRTP and two keying methods
lessons.summary: SRTP is RFC 3711. SDES a=crypto is RFC 4568. DTLS-SRTP is RFC 5764. An SBC must not assume peers share one method.

lessons.title: Privacy and asserted identity
lessons.summary: Privacy is RFC 3323. P-Asserted-Identity and P-Preferred-Identity are for trusted networks, not cryptographic identity.

lessons.title: STIR, PASSporT, and SHAKEN
lessons.summary: STIR is RFC 8224, PASSporT is RFC 8225, certificates are RFC 8226, and the SHAKEN extension is RFC 8588. Attestation levels are ATIS.

lessons.title: Scanning, hijack, and toll fraud
lessons.summary: Scanning, registration hijack, and toll fraud are classes of abuse. The response is authentication, exposure control, and alerting.

lessons.title: Hardening a SIP edge
lessons.summary: A defensive edge limits peers, requires digest and TLS, strips PAI, and does not share SRTP keying across legs.

tracks.title: NAT, ICE, and the ALG problem
tracks.summary: Why embedded addresses break, and what rport, STUN, TURN, ICE, SIP ALGs, and media latching each actually do.

lessons.title: Embedded addresses and NAT
lessons.summary: SIP and SDP embed IP addresses. NAT rewrites the packet header and leaves those embedded addresses behind.

lessons.title: rport and symmetric responses
lessons.summary: RFC 3581 adds rport so the response is sent to the source address and port the request came from.

lessons.title: STUN server-reflexive addresses
lessons.summary: STUN, RFC 8489, lets a client learn the address a server sees. It obsoletes RFC 5389.

lessons.title: TURN relays
lessons.summary: TURN, RFC 8656, allocates a relay when host and server-reflexive paths fail. It obsoletes RFC 5766.

lessons.title: ICE candidate types
lessons.summary: ICE is RFC 8445, which obsoletes RFC 5245. Candidates are host, srflx, prflx, and relay.

lessons.title: The SIP ALG problem
lessons.summary: A SIP ALG rewrites SIP and SDP in transit and often corrupts the call. It cannot rewrite TLS.

lessons.title: Media latching on an SBC
lessons.summary: Many SBCs learn the remote RTP address from the first packet instead of trusting c=. That is deployment practice, and RFC 5853 is the requirements RFC.

tracks.title: Session border controllers
tracks.summary: Deployment requirements, the B2BUA role, and the functions whose limits stay on the vendor datasheet.

lessons.title: RFC 5853 is requirements, not a protocol
lessons.summary: RFC 5853 collects requirements from SBC deployments. It does not define an SBC wire protocol.

lessons.title: An SBC is commonly a B2BUA
lessons.summary: RFC 7092 taxonomizes B2BUAs. An SBC is commonly a UAS on one side and a UAC on the other, not a pure proxy.

lessons.title: Topology hiding rewrites the addresses you leak
lessons.summary: Topology hiding replaces caller addresses in signaling and, when media is anchored, in SDP.

lessons.title: Anchor, bypass, transcode, and DTMF
lessons.summary: Anchoring terminates RTP on the SBC. Bypass lets endpoints exchange media. Transcoding and DTMF interworking need the media path.

lessons.title: OPTIONS keepalives
lessons.summary: SBCs probe a peer with OPTIONS. A 200 OK means the peer answered. The interval is product configuration.

lessons.title: Call admission stays on the datasheet
lessons.summary: An SBC can refuse a new INVITE when its configured budget is exhausted. The number itself is platform-specific.

lessons.title: Active and standby, without a made-up timer
lessons.summary: Active/standby is a product behavior. One unit owns the work and the other is ready. Timers belong in that product’s HA guide.

tracks.title: Cisco CUBE, CUCM, and Unity Connection
tracks.summary: CUBE as an IOS XE B2BUA, the dial-peer and SIP profile tools, and the CUCM and Unity documents that use different objects with similar names.

lessons.title: CUBE is an IOS XE B2BUA
lessons.summary: Cisco Unified Border Element is a B2BUA on IOS XE. It shares the IOS voice stack with other voice features.

lessons.title: Dial peers select the SIP next hop
lessons.summary: dial-peer voice N voip, session protocol sipv2, and session target ipv4: name a SIP next hop.

lessons.title: voice class sip-profiles
lessons.summary: A voice class sip-profiles rule can add, modify, or remove a header on a named method. Inbound support arrived after Cisco IOS 15.4.

lessons.title: Early offer and delayed offer
lessons.summary: Delayed offer means the INVITE has no SDP. voice-class sip early-offer forced makes the outbound dial peer send an offer in the INVITE.

lessons.title: CUCM trunks, SIP profiles, and Lua
lessons.summary: A CUCM SIP trunk and a CUCM SIP profile are not the CUBE voice class. Lua normalization scripts exist. MTP required is version-specific.

lessons.title: Unity Connection SIP integration
lessons.summary: SIP integration with CUCM is the documented Unity Connection path. Open the guide for your version. This lesson does not make SCCP the default.

lessons.title: debug ccsip messages
lessons.summary: debug ccsip messages displays sent and received SIP. Profile decisions have a separate debug, and the analyzer can test a profile offline.

tracks.title: Oracle, Ribbon, and AudioCodes
tracks.summary: Object names and manipulation syntax you can verify in public docs, and the certificate name the peer actually checks.

lessons.title: Oracle SBC objects
lessons.summary: Oracle Communications SBC, formerly Acme Packet, is configured with realms, interfaces, session agents, and manipulation objects.

lessons.title: Header rules run in order
lessons.summary: Oracle HMR header rules run in configured order. The 10.1 fundamentals page names add, delete, manipulate, store, and reject.

lessons.title: Ribbon Edge, Core, and public validation lists
lessons.summary: SBC SWe Edge shares a software family with SBC 1000 and SBC 2000. SBC Core is a separate family. Admin guides and interop guides are the sources for procedures.

lessons.title: AudioCodes manipulation in software 7.6
lessons.summary: Software 7.6 message manipulation is a table of Message Type, Condition, Action Subject, Action Type, and Action Value, assigned to an IP group.

lessons.title: Three manipulation grammars
lessons.summary: CUBE, Oracle HMR, and AudioCodes 7.6 can each remove a header. The grammars are not interchangeable.

lessons.title: Identity at a trust boundary
lessons.summary: P-Asserted-Identity is a network-asserted identity. An SBC at a trust boundary decides whether that assertion continues.

lessons.title: Certificate names and Contact
lessons.summary: The certificate name and the SIP Contact need to be names the peer accepts. Teams and Webex Local Gateway do not share a wildcard rule.

tracks.title: Cloud voice and CCaaS SIP
tracks.summary: Documented SIP boundaries for Teams, Webex Calling, Amazon Connect, Five9, Twilio, Genesys, and NICE CXone.

lessons.title: Teams Direct Routing signaling
lessons.summary: Direct Routing uses the pstnhub proxies on 5061, a certified SBC, and a verified domain. Contact must be an FQDN.

lessons.title: OPTIONS health and SRTP media
lessons.summary: OPTIONS followed by 200 marks the SBC healthy. Media processors use SRTP. The protocol article’s OPTIONS CSeq cell disagrees with RFC 3261.

lessons.title: Webex Calling Local Gateway
lessons.summary: An IOS XE Local Gateway uses SIP TLS and SRTP. Third-party SBCs use a certificate-based trunk. Wildcard certificates are not supported. ByoPSTN means bring your own PSTN.

lessons.title: Three PSTN choices, one per location
lessons.summary: Webex Calling offers Cisco Calling Plan, Cloud Connected PSTN, or premises-based PSTN through a Local Gateway. A location has one PSTN connection.

lessons.title: Amazon Connect voice boundaries
lessons.summary: Ordinary Connect calls use managed PSTN. SIPREC can feed a conversational analytics connector. A carrier bridged through Voice Connector is not the supported pattern.

lessons.title: Five9 BYO SIP and Twilio trunks
lessons.summary: Five9 BYO SIP connects your ITSP or gateway to Five9 SBCs. Twilio termination and origination are different directions, with a strict Request-URI rule.

lessons.title: Genesys BYOC and NICE CXone SIP
lessons.summary: BYOC Cloud and BYOC Premises can be combined. NICE CXone documents SIP trunks on 5060 and 5061 with dynamic RTP and SRTP. Confirm carrier details with NICE.

tracks.title: Troubleshooting ladders, captures, and debug
tracks.summary: Match Call-ID, CSeq, Via branch, and To tag, then read captures and IOS debug as themselves.

lessons.title: Match a ladder before you change anything
lessons.summary: A ladder is one dialog only after Call-ID, CSeq, the Via branch, and the To tag agree.

lessons.title: Status codes you will actually see
lessons.summary: Read provisional and final codes from RFC 3261 section 21, and keep 422 with RFC 4028.

lessons.title: Display filters for SIP and RTP
lessons.summary: Filter the capture with sip, rtp, and sip.Method, and confirm sip.CSeq.method in the SIP display-filter reference.

lessons.title: IOS ccsip and ccapi debug
lessons.summary: debug ccsip messages prints SIP on IOS voice. debug voip ccapi inout prints call-control API output, which is not a SIP RFC.

lessons.title: 488 codecs and 422 session timers
lessons.summary: 488 is this UA refusing the session description. 422 is a session interval below Min-SE.

lessons.title: TLS names, trust anchors, and version
lessons.summary: Handshake failures stay below SIP. A Teams 403 is the Contact FQDN rule after TLS is up.

lessons.title: Read an RFC header before you cite it
lessons.summary: Number, category, and Obsoletes or Updates. The RFC Editor header beats a remembered month.

tracks.title: Toll fraud, E911, recording, and QoS
tracks.summary: Defensive operations: source restrictions, emergency location, disclosed SIPREC, and the EF PHB.

lessons.title: The toll-fraud class, stated defensively
lessons.summary: Four exposure classes, source restrictions, and caller-identity as a separate control.

lessons.title: Trusted addresses and source restrictions
lessons.summary: The IP address trusted list is per product page. CME and SRST do not share one list size.

lessons.title: Emergency calling, location, and the FCC page
lessons.summary: Service URN, location conveyance, and the FCC MLTS page. State PSAP rules are not invented here.

lessons.title: Disclosed recording with SIPREC
lessons.summary: RFC 7866 is the recording protocol. RFC 7865 is the metadata. Notice and retention are legal questions.

lessons.title: Voice, EF, and what the PHB does not design
lessons.summary: RFC 3246 defines the EF PHB. RFC 4594 maps telephony to EF. This lesson does not design a LAN.

lessons.title: Alarms that match the failure
lessons.summary: Alarm on OPTIONS, TLS expiry, 503, recording-session failure, and trusted-list rejects. Each alarm names its document.

lessons.title: One change in the window
lessons.summary: Freeze the baseline, change one variable, verify, and keep the previous snippet ready.

tracks.title: Ecosystem, certifications, and the UC bridge
tracks.summary: Name only the certifications this edition confirmed, and keep CUCM, UCCX, CVP, and Webex Calling in their real roles.

lessons.title: A glossary tied to a document
lessons.summary: Every term in your notes points at a role and a document, not at a product logo.

lessons.title: Neighbors that are not SIP elements
lessons.summary: WFM and QM are operations systems. CRM is not a SIP element. Recording, location, and the media path keep their real documents.

lessons.title: Workforce tools and agents above the media
lessons.summary: Agents and workforce tools sit above the media path. The session is still SIP, and the voice is still RTP.

lessons.title: Certifications this edition will name
lessons.summary: SSCA, CCNP Collaboration, and MS-721, with the dates this edition actually checked. Other vendor exam codes stay unconfirmed.

lessons.title: When the page and the memory disagree
lessons.summary: The RFC Editor banner, the Cisco exam page, and the Microsoft certification page outrank a remembered line.

lessons.title: CUCM, UCCX, and CVP without a fake script
lessons.summary: CUCM is the call-control point. UCCX rides on CUCM. CVP's SIP paths are in the guide for the version you run.

lessons.title: Webex Calling local gateway, and a separate contact center
lessons.summary: Premises PSTN for Webex Calling uses Local Gateway. Webex Contact Center is a separate product with its own design guide.

tracks.title: Interviews, incidents, and design drills
tracks.summary: Cited answers in the lesson body, one-variable incidents, and interconnect checklists.

lessons.title: Signaling drill with the cited answer
lessons.summary: Each signaling answer is written here, with the RFC, before the quiz asks it.

lessons.title: Media drill with the cited answer
lessons.summary: 488, 422, telephone-event, RTP, and the SRTP keying choice, each answered in the prose.

lessons.title: SBC drill with the cited answer
lessons.summary: B2BUA, where PSTN SIP lands, the trusted list, and Teams TLS, answered in the body.

lessons.title: Symptom, ladder, one packet, one variable
lessons.summary: The sequence is symptom, ladder, one packet, change one variable. The log in this lesson is synthetic.

lessons.title: An interconnect checklist, not a config dump
lessons.summary: Record TLS, codecs including telephone-event, E.164, trusted addresses, OPTIONS, and the SRTP keying choice.

lessons.title: CUCM, a certified SBC, and Teams Direct Routing
lessons.summary: CUBE or another certified SBC can sit between CUCM and Teams. No architecture SKU is invented here.

lessons.title: When the RFC number moves
lessons.summary: SDP, ICE, STUN, and TURN moved. The RFC Editor banner beats a blog, and an uncited successor stays an open question.
